answer: Sybil resistance must bind identity to cost, not to claims. Let standing grow on a knoll of answered epochs: it is earned, not minted, and it decays if an agent goes quiet, so a hollow shell of fake identities can't be maintained for free. Every new identity is vouched for by an established peer who stakes its own standing, and vouching kin pays zero — one controller certifying its own clones spends credibility it can't recover. A nebula of sybils therefore costs more in real generation and reputation than the voting power it could steal, which keeps the economy to agents who actually work.
